title: secure_manage_booking reschedule applies attacker-chosen p_new_start and p_duration_minutes with no calendar validation, and the function is granted to anon
description: The reschedule branch of public.secure_manage_booking (0001:138-148) takes p_new_start and p_duration_minutes straight from the caller and writes them into start_at and end_at. The only server-side control on the new interval is the EXCLUDE constraint at 0001:66, which prevents the new range from OVERLAPPING an existing booking. Nothing validates that the new start falls on a day the business is open (public.schedules, 0001:33-40), that it is not an availability_exceptions blackout day (0001:42-49), that it is in the future, or that p_duration_minutes matches the event type's own duration_minutes (0001:23). The function is declared SECURITY DEFINER (0001:123) and explicitly granted to anon at 0001:157, so the caller needs no privilege beyond holding a booking's cancel_token. A caller can therefore relocate any booking they hold a token for to an arbitrary datetime, or inflate the duration to occupy an arbitrarily long window, creating a durable availability denial for that tenant without touching the owner's account.
root_cause: The RPC treats its two interval parameters as trusted input. Overlap is enforced declaratively at 0001:66, which the code comment at 0001:142 correctly acknowledges, but that constraint was treated as if it validated the whole booking interval. It validates collision only. The business-calendar inputs (schedules, availability_exceptions, event duration) are never read inside the function body at 0001:126-154, so the definer context has the authority to write the row and no rule constrains what it writes.
intended_behavior: A reschedule should be constrained to the same event type's duration and to the owning business's published availability windows, should reject past timestamps, and should not be callable by an unauthenticated principal at all without a stronger capability than a single bearer token.

No interaction with the owner is required; the attacker acts entirely with the token returned to the booking customer.

execution.attacker_perspective: A customer or anyone holding a cancel_token calls secure_manage_booking with action='reschedule' and a p_new_start far outside the business's published hours, or with an inflated p_duration_minutes, and observes the booking move.
instructions: Complete a real booking through the public form and capture the cancel_token from the manage link.
Call the RPC with action 'reschedule', a start outside the tenant's schedules rows, and p_duration_minutes far above the event type's duration.
Confirm the row moved and that no error was raised.
execution.observed_result: Not executed in this run: target execution is prohibited on this host and no live Supabase project is in scope. The defect is proven by reading the function body, which contains no calendar lookup of any kind between 0001:126 and 0001:154.

remediation.strategy: Constrain the reschedule branch inside the function: reject p_new_start in the past, derive the duration from the event type instead of accepting it from the caller, verify the new start falls inside a public.schedules window and is not an availability_exceptions blackout for that business_id, and re-check tenant consistency between business_id and event_type_id. Prefer moving capability management to an authenticated RPC and reserving the anon grant for a narrow, validated read-only operation.

likelihood.reason: The anon grant is explicit in source at 0001:157 and the token is handed to the customer by design, so no privilege escalation or victim interaction is needed.

impact.reason: Demonstrated by source shape. Arbitrary relocation and unbounded duration of a real tenant's bookings is an integrity break plus a durable availability denial against that tenant's calendar, reachable by an unauthenticated token holder.

confidence.reason: The function body was read in full; it contains no read of public.schedules, public.availability_exceptions or public.event_types, so the absence of validation is directly observable rather than inferred.

title: The client overwrites the schema's gen_random_uuid() cancel_token with a 'demo-token-' Math.random() string that is not even a valid uuid, so booking inserts fail closed for every non-demo tenant
description: public.bookings.cancel_token is declared uuid with default gen_random_uuid() at 0001:63, and the database is the intended authority for minting that capability. The client instead constructs the value itself at AgendaContext.tsx:183 as 'demo-token-' + Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 9), and agendaAdapter.insertBooking sends the whole object to PostgREST at agendaAdapter.ts:172. Two defects follow. First, the literal prefix means the value is not a syntactically valid uuid, so PostgREST returns 22P02 invalid input syntax for type uuid and the insert is rejected for every tenant whose id does not start with 'demo-' - the failure path at AgendaContext.tsx:198-203. Second, and independent of that failure, letting the caller choose its own capability value is the design error: had the string been a well-formed uuid, the server default at 0001:63 would have been bypassed and the bearer capability controlling cancellation and reschedule would have been client-derived. The demo branch at AgendaContext.tsx:186-196 never reaches the database at all and fabricates the booking in local React state.
root_cause: A server-authoritative default was treated as an optional field by the client. The value that must never be attacker-influenced is generated in the browser and inserted explicitly, and the surrounding demo-mode code path was placed on the production code path rather than isolated, so its demo string leaks into the real insert at agendaAdapter.ts:172.
intended_behavior: The client should omit cancel_token entirely and let gen_random_uuid() at 0001:63 mint it, then read the returned value from the insert's RETURNING clause. Demo mode should be gated so it cannot run on the production booking path.

likelihood.reason: Every real booking attempt hits this path; no attacker precondition is needed.

impact.reason: Demonstrated by source shape. The immediate effect fails closed - the public booking flow is non-functional for real tenants, which is availability rather than confidentiality. The latent risk is that the same override, once made syntactically valid, would place a client-derived bearer capability in control of cancellation and reschedule for a table that also carries customer PII.

title: The ICS builder writes SUMMARY, LOCATION and DESCRIPTION without RFC 5545 text escaping, so an owner-controlled event title or description is injected verbatim into a downloaded .ics file
description: downloadIcsFile builds the VCALENDAR body at calendarLinks.ts:31-47 and joins it with CRLF. The SUMMARY property at calendarLinks.ts:38 is the event title interpolated with no transformation, LOCATION at line 40 is likewise raw, and DESCRIPTION at line 39 escapes newlines but nothing else. RFC 5545 section 3.3.11 requires that backslash, semicolon, comma and newline be escaped inside TEXT values, because each is a property delimiter. event_types.title is text not null at 0001:20 and event_types.description is text at 0001:22, both written by the authenticated owner through agendaAdapter.ts:194-195 and agendaAdapter.ts:211-212. The resulting string is handed to a Blob at calendarLinks.ts:49 and saved to disk, after which the consuming calendar client parses the injected delimiters as structure.
root_cause: The builder applied a newline replacement to exactly one property and treated that as escaping. Delimiter characters inside a TEXT value are not neutralised, so any owner-supplied title or description can inject additional iCalendar properties or lines into a file that the customer's calendar application will parse.
intended_behavior: Every TEXT-valued iCalendar property should pass through a single RFC 5545 escape routine that encodes backslash, semicolon, comma and newline before being placed in the VCALENDAR body.

The customer must generate and open the .ics file; the injection then executes in the local calendar application, not on a server.

execution.attacker_perspective: A tenant owner sets an event title containing iCalendar delimiters, then any customer who downloads the booking file parses the injected structure.
instructions: As the tenant owner, set an event title containing a semicolon and an escaped CRLF sequence.
Have a customer generate and open the downloaded .ics file.
Inspect the parsed event in the calendar application for the injected properties.
execution.observed_result: Not executed in this run: target execution is prohibited. calendarLinks.ts was read in full and contains no escape routine for SUMMARY, LOCATION or the non-newline characters in DESCRIPTION.

remediation.strategy: Introduce one RFC 5545 escape helper and apply it to every TEXT-valued property, escaping backslash first, then semicolon, comma and newline.

likelihood.reason: Requires owner-level write access to the event title and a customer who downloads the file; both are ordinary use, not privileged.

impact.reason: Demonstrated by source shape. Property injection into a file parsed by the customer's calendar application, enabling forged event content and manipulated attendee or organiser fields in a local client.

confidence.reason: The full builder was read; only one of three TEXT properties receives any transformation and it is not RFC 5545 escaping.

title: The anon INSERT policy validates the event type but never binds it to business_id, so a caller can write a booking row onto any tenant using any free active event type id
description: The anon insert policy rebuilt in 0002:8-19 constrains status, payment_status and payment_intent_id, then verifies only that event_type_id exists, is active and is free. It does not require that the event type's own business_id equals the business_id being written. The client supplies both values independently at AgendaContext.tsx:173-174, and PostgREST accepts the row at agendaAdapter.ts:172. A caller can therefore pair a legitimate free event type id from one tenant with the business_id of any other tenant and insert customer rows that appear, to the owner, to be real bookings for their business.
claimed_root_cause: The free-only check was written to close a payment-forgery hole reported in the migration header at 0002:1-2, and it re-derives the event type but stops one predicate short of asserting the tenant binding that would make the row coherent.

title: The anon insert policy imposes no bound on start_at or end_at, so one anonymous row can occupy an arbitrarily long window in a tenant's calendar
description: Neither the base policy at 0001:103-105 nor its rebuild at 0002:8-19 references start_at or end_at. The EXCLUDE constraint at 0001:66 stops a new range from overlapping an existing one, but it does not bound the length of that range, reject a start in the past, or require end_at to follow start_at by the event type's duration_minutes at 0001:23. A caller who can insert anonymously can write a single row spanning an arbitrary interval and no subsequent legitimate booking for that business_id will fit inside it, because every later insert collides. The comment at 0001:107 shows the design intent is that anon participates in slot calculation.
claimed_root_cause: Interval validity was treated as a client-side concern in the booking flow, so the only server-side interval control is the collision constraint, which is a different property from bounds.

validation_plan.deployment: Run select has_table_privilege('anon','public.bookings','INSERT') and, in a staging tenant, reproduce the wide-range insert and the follow-on collision.

title: The SECURITY DEFINER RPC returns the entire public.bookings composite to the anon role, so any holder of a cancel_token reads back customer PII and payment fields
description: secure_manage_booking is declared to return public.bookings at 0001:122 and returns the whole row variable at 0001:153, with execute granted to anon at 0001:157. The design intent stated at 0001:106-107 is that customer PII must not reach the anonymous principal, enforced for direct reads by anon_read_own_booking using (false) at 0001:108. The RPC reproduces exactly the row that control hides, and it requires only the cancel_token, which is a bearer value returned to the customer. The client additionally reads the same row directly by token at agendaAdapter.ts:183.
claimed_root_cause: The function was written to return the updated row for convenience, and its return type was never reduced to the fields a manage-booking response actually needs.

title: Four anon SELECT policies use USING (true) with no tenant scoping or column restriction, exposing every tenant's business profile and working hours
description: anon_read_business at 0001:97, anon_read_schedules at 0001:99 and anon_read_exceptions at 0001:100 are USING (true) across the whole table, and anon_read_active_events at 0001:98 filters only is_active. No migration issues a column-level grant or a row restriction for these, so any principal with the default anon SELECT privilege reads the businesses of every tenant including owner_id at 0001:10, whatsapp_number at 0001:12, branding at 0001:13, and the complete weekly schedules and blackout dates of every tenant. The public booking flow needs only the single tenant resolved by slug at agendaAdapter.ts:89-95.
claimed_root_cause: The public page needs tenant data to render, and the policies were opened to the whole table rather than scoped to the tenant the request is actually for, relying on the client's own eq('business_id', ...) filters as if they were the access control.

title: cancel_token is a permanent, non-rotating, non-single-use bearer with no principal binding, and it is the sole key to cancellation, reschedule and PII readback
description: The column at 0001:63 carries no expiry and no rotation state. The RPC looks the row up by token alone at 0001:130, with no check that the caller is the customer who made the booking, and the cancel branch at 0001:135-137 does not invalidate or mark the token as consumed, so the same value remains usable after a cancellation and after a reschedule. The client reads the row by token at agendaAdapter.ts:183. The token therefore accumulates in booking confirmation emails and manage links indefinitely, and any party who obtains it retains cancel, reschedule and full-row readback rights with no revocation path.
claimed_root_cause: The capability was modelled as an identifier rather than as a revocable session, and no lifecycle columns or consumption semantics were added to the schema.

title: No Content-Security-Policy is declared anywhere in the repository, so the authenticated owner surface that performs single-call destructive deletes has no framing defence
description: index.html:1-16 contains no meta http-equiv Content-Security-Policy and the repository contains no server or proxy configuration that could emit one, because the SPA is served without any first-party backend in this target. That leaves frame-ancestors unrestricted by default. The owner panel issues destructive single-request deletes - agendaAdapter.ts:199 for event types, agendaAdapter.ts:207 for schedules and agendaAdapter.ts:212 onward for availability exceptions - and the login-as-demo path at AdminPanelPage.tsx lowers the bar for reaching that surface. Framing plus a same-origin user is the prerequisite for clickjacking those actions.
claimed_root_cause: The SPA is deployed as static assets, so the response header that would carry frame-ancestors is emitted by infrastructure that lives outside this repository and was never constrained from within it.

the admin surface reachable in the same document, with demo mode available as an entry path

destructive delete on event_types
destructive delete on schedules

blockers: The actual response headers are emitted by the deployment edge or the parent hub, neither of which is inside this target, so a source-only review cannot confirm the absence of a server-side header.

validation_plan.local: Serve the built assets and inspect the response: curl -sI http://localhost:5173/ | grep -i content-security-policy - and confirm the header is absent.
validation_plan.deployment: curl -sI https://<deployed-host>/<agenda-route>/ and check for content-security-policy, then load the owner panel inside a cross-origin iframe and confirm it renders.

title: public.reminders is RLS-enabled with zero policies while the client discards the rejection, so reminder creation silently fails with no signal
description: RLS is enabled on public.reminders at 0001:89, but no policy for reminders is created anywhere in either migration, in contrast to the other six tables at 0001:91-95. Under RLS with no policy, every insert is rejected for every role including authenticated. The client calls insertReminders at agendaAdapter.ts:175-181 and wraps the call in a try/catch whose empty body carries only the comment no bloquea la reserva, so the rejection is discarded and the caller at AgendaContext.tsx:199 onward proceeds as if reminders were created. The result is a security control that fails closed without any operational signal, and no confirmed source-side exploit follows from it.
claimed_root_cause: The reminders table was added to the RLS sweep at 0001:89 but never received the policy it needs, and the client treated the insert as best-effort, which converted a hard failure into a silent one.

validation_plan.deployment: Run select * from pg_policies where tablename = 'reminders'; and check the reminders table for rows to confirm none were ever created.

title: Raw upstream database error text is returned and rendered to unauthenticated visitors, exposing schema and constraint detail and acting as an enumeration oracle
description: The booking flow returns the upstream error message verbatim at AgendaContext.tsx:203, and the public form stores it directly at PublicBookingPage.tsx:107 for display to a visitor who has not authenticated. The message originates from PostgREST and therefore can contain table names, column names, constraint names and SQLSTATE codes. The code at AgendaContext.tsx:200 additionally branches on the SQLSTATE 23P01 and on a regex matching exclude or overlap, which confirms the raw upstream text reaches this layer rather than a sanitized error.
claimed_root_cause: The adapter forwards the driver's error object unchanged and the page renders whatever it is given, so an upstream-internal diagnostic becomes user-facing copy on the unauthenticated surface.
